summary: Construction, improvement and repair of real property are not taxed to the owner in Wyoming; the contractor pays sales or use tax on the materials it uses.

citations.title: Wyoming DOR Excise Tax Division bulletin, Contractor (last revised August 2026)
citations.quote: Charges for labor to alter, improve or construct real property are not subject to sales/use tax, unless performed within an oil or gas wellsite.

citations.title: Wyoming DOR Excise Tax Division bulletin, Contractor (last revised August 2026)
citations.quote: Any contractor who furnishes tangible personal property in the construction, alteration, improvement or repair of real property is the consumer or user of tangible personal property within the meaning of the sales and use tax laws of Wyoming.

citations.title: W.S. 39-15-205 (local sales and use taxes: exemptions)
citations.quote: There are no specific applicable provisions for exemptions for this article. The provisions of W.S. 39-15-105 shall apply to the taxes imposed by this article.

notes: The labor sentence names alteration, improvement and construction; repair labor on real property is not an enumerated taxable service (only repair of tangible personal property is, W.S. 39-15-103(a)(i)(J)), and the contractor is the consumer of materials for repairs too, so repair is treated the same. Work within an oil or gas well site is taxable (W.S. 39-15-103(a)(i)(K)). The earliest dated copy read is the bulletin as revised August 2026; the treatment is likely older (the bulletin was first issued earlier) but no earlier copy was read. County, city and resort-district sales taxes (W.S. 39-15-204) are levied on the same retail sales and take the state's exemptions (W.S. 39-15-205), so one WY rule covers state and local parts. Wyoming's 2026 SF0079 (Enrolled Act 018, effective 2026-07-01) reorganized the sales/use tax statutes; the DOR bulletins (revised August 2026) still cite the earlier section numbers. Treatment is unchanged as far as the bulletins show.

summary: A separately stated charge for delivering goods to the buyer (outbound freight) is not subject to Wyoming sales tax.

citations.quote: Both intrastate (instate) and interstate (state-to-state) outbound freight is exempt from Wyoming sales tax provided it is separately stated and distinguishable from any taxable charges that may appear on the same invoice.

citations.title: Wyoming DOR Excise Tax Division bulletin, Freight and Transportation Charges (last revised August 2026): Rules ch. 2 sec. 5(i)
citations.quote: Transportation or outbound freight charges are not taxable and shall not be included within the taxable sales price of any retail sale.

citations.title: Wyoming DOR bulletin, Freight and Transportation Charges (revised August 1, 2014; archived 2017-01-19)
citations.quote: outbound freight is exempt from Wyoming sales tax provided it is separately stated and distinguishable from any taxable charges

citations.quote: There are no specific applicable provisions for exemptions for this article. The provisions of W.S. 39-15-105 shall apply to the taxes imposed by this article.

notes: Inbound freight the seller passes on (e.g. a dealer's delivery charge for bringing goods to its store) is part of the taxable price even when itemized; a delivery charge not separately stated is taxed with the goods. County, city and resort-district sales taxes (W.S. 39-15-204) are levied on the same retail sales and take the state's exemptions (W.S. 39-15-205), so one WY rule covers state and local parts. Treatment is unchanged as far as the bulletins show.

Wyoming's 2026 SF0079 (Enrolled Act 018, effective 2026-07-01) reorganized the sales/use tax statutes; the DOR bulletins (revised August 2026) still cite the earlier section numbers. Treatment is unchanged as far as the bulletins show.

summary: Custom software, and a separately stated charge for customizing prewritten software, are not subject to Wyoming sales tax.

citations.title: Wyoming DOR Excise Tax Division bulletin, Computer Sales & Services (last revised August 2026)
citations.quote: The sale of custom software, delivered electronically or otherwise, is not subject to sales tax nor is the creation of such software.

citations.title: Wyoming DOR Excise Tax Division bulletin, Computer Sales & Services (last revised August 2026)
citations.quote: In such case, the prewritten portion would be taxable and the separate charge for the modification or enhancement would not be taxable.

citations.title: W.S. 39-15-205 (local sales and use taxes: exemptions)
citations.quote: There are no specific applicable provisions for exemptions for this article. The provisions of W.S. 39-15-105 shall apply to the taxes imposed by this article.

notes: A modification not separately stated from the prewritten software remains prewritten and taxable; installing software is a taxable service. summary: Prewritten software is tangible personal property in Wyoming and taxable however it is delivered, including downloads.

citations.title: Wyoming DOR Excise Tax Division bulletin, Computer Sales & Services (last revised August 2026)
citations.quote: Please be aware that sales of prewritten computer software are taxable regardless of the delivery method.

summary: Software as a service (remote access without receiving a copy) is not subject to Wyoming sales tax.

citations.title: Wyoming DOR Excise Tax Division bulletin, Computer Sales & Services (last revised August 2026)
citations.quote: are not subject to Wyoming sales tax provided the customer does not receive any tangible personal property or enumerated service embedded within the service.
